problem: The demand is written per node ('each node must send one 10 Gb/s lightpath to each of the other five'), which is 6 × 5 = 30 directed demands, but the traffic is then summed over the 15 undirected pairs. A 10 Gb/s lightpath normally carries 10 Gb/s in each direction, so a student counting node by node writes 300 Gb/s while the answer says 150 Gb/s. The same mismatch appears in Quiz Q3.
fix: State the convention: 'Each pair exchanges 10 Gb/s in each direction; the working traffic is 150 Gb/s in each direction, 300 Gb/s counting both directions.' Apply the same wording to Q3 (100 Gb/s each direction, 200 Gb/s both directions).

problem: 'A span is one amplified section inside a link' is only one usage. Many textbooks use span and link as synonyms (the fiber between two adjacent nodes), so the later trap 'Link, span, path and channel are not synonyms' can contradict what a student reads elsewhere. Also, the power budget in Unit 5 applies to the whole transmitter-to-receiver link, not to one span alone.
fix: 'A link may contain several spans; a span is the amplified section between two amplifiers (some textbooks use span for the whole link). Each span's loss must fit the amplifier and power budget.'

problem: Saying 'some syllabi call it a wavelength path or an optical channel' collides with the chapter's own definition of a channel as one wavelength on one link, so the two terms look contradictory to a student.
fix: Keep 'wavelength path' and add: 'some books also say wavelength channel; do not confuse this end-to-end meaning with a channel in the earlier one-link sense.'

problem: 'Protection doubles both wavelengths and transponders' is stated as a general rule, but the chapter itself says 1:N uses one backup for N working paths, and on a ring with no wavelength reuse the protection route is link-disjoint, so the working wavelength can be reused there. Only the transponder count always doubles; the wavelength count doubles only for dedicated 1+1 under a separate-wavelength assignment.
fix: 'Under 1+1 with a separate wavelength per lightpath, the wavelength count and the transponder count both double. 1:N shares one backup among N working paths, so the extra capacity is not N times. Count the second copy on every link of the protection path, not on one link only.'
